newsitem.title: INDIA: India Shaw Wallace to repay debt.
newsitem.headline: India Shaw Wallace to repay debt.

text.p: Indian liquor maker Shaw Wallace and Company said on Friday that its board had approved a financing plan to repay all its debts in two or three years.

"The board discussed the financial plan drawn up by the management and approved it," the company said in a statement. "With strong current earnings, the board felt confident of being able to pay off all its outstandings within two to three years."
The statement said the company was considering bids to sell its consumer products division comprising of Calcutta Chemicals Co and Detergents India Ltd.
It was also considering bids to sell its Neem, Aramusk and Margo soap brands. Selling its Chek detergent and Tuhina cough syrup brand were also under consideration.

The statement said the company's accounts for 1996/97 would be completed shortly. The statement gave no details about the amount of the outstanding debt. It also did not specify the price at which various brands would be sold.
